description: Frozen fresh interview: exact program plan and retained drafts. Diagnostic regression only; no fresh-song qualification claimed.

density.chosen_from: uniform over 1..4 per PLAN (the line-binding ceiling), from a stream seeded on (seed, 'density'); each line then draws its participation uniform over 1..3, and the end-rhyme pass binds free line ends on top (M-191)

end_rhyme.chosen_from: NOT A DRAW — each sung section's own `schemes[fn].rgs` re-realised at the line ends, so this consumes no seed entropy and the placement draw above is untouched. Three counts, never summed (doctrine 79): `added` groups emitted; `blocked` blocks whose ends the placement draw had already spent; `narrow` blocks whose lines cannot carry one more DISTINCT word.

execution.basis: registry span enumeration; no phonological bucket pruning assumed
execution.scope: English lines at or below the declared density ceiling; no latency/RSS guarantee

meter.chosen_from: 178 derived cycles (beats envelope [2, 12], slots envelope [5, 48]), measured BY DERIVATION ON THE DECLARED COORDINATE: 1 of 11 beats-per-line values, then 1 of 2 bars x subdivision factorisation(s) of 3 beats, then 1 of 1 groupings of 3. The line runs 3 beat(s) — at most the density band's ceiling, since a sung line carries at least one syllable a beat — and holds 12 slot(s), at least the band's floor. Both ends are the same calibrated band in different units; the pair share follows from how many ways each beat count factorises. Unit is notation, never enforced

narrative.chosen_from: uniform over the 1086 legal story line-ups of this shape (quality/narrative.py, M-121; the count is exact and the draw is entropy-last)

pattern.chosen_from: generated grammar: 22 cell types x 1..7 cells under the drawn total and declared brief, optional intro/outro/coda, roster 20 of 22 functions

placements.measure: uniform per MEMBER over the pool; per member and not per group because 8 of the 77 registered schemas anchor one member at each end of a word
placements.token_ceiling_from: the smaller of the floor's measured tokens-per-line floor 7.00 and this plan's own shortest line (9 syllable(s) after its pickup) less one for the last word — a plan asks for the n-th word only where BOTH the calibration and this meter say a line carries that many

relations.chosen_from: NOT DRAWN — the writer declared --relation and a declared coordinate is carried, never sampled over (M-55)

execution_limits.basis: registry span enumeration; no phonological bucket pruning assumed
execution_limits.scope: English lines at or below the declared density ceiling; no latency/RSS guarantee

plan.title: Dead Letter Office
plan.writer_brief:
Write a song: 28 lines, 5 sections, in this order:
  [CHORUS — 5 lines — 5 bars of 3/8, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 9 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 5 lines — 5 bars of 3/8, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 9 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [BRIDGE — 10 lines — 10 bars of 3/8, half-beat pickup]
      up to 10 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [VERSE — 4 lines — 4 bars of 3/8, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 9 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [VERSE — 4 lines — 4 bars of 3/8, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 9 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
Feel: 3/8 grouped 3.
Rhyme plan (line numbers over the whole song):
  lines 1.headrime & 2.headrime & 3.endword stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 1.T2 & 4 & 5.T7 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 2.T3 & 3.head stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 11.T7 & 12.T1 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 13.endword & 16.T5 & 18.T4 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 14.T2 & 15.T2 & 17.endword stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 12.T4 & 13.T2 & 14.T4 & 15 & 16.T7 & 19.endword & 20 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 13.headrime & 14.endword & 19.T7 & 20.T1 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 19.T4 & 20.T2 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 21.T3 & 22.T7 & 23.T5 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 21.head & 24.T4 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 21.T4 & 24.T5 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 25.T3 & 26.head & 27.T7 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 26.T7 & 27.T3 & 28.headrime stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 1 & 2 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 11 & 12 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 16 & 18 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 21 & 22 & 23 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 25 & 26 & 27 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
Story plan (one job per sung section; each enters from the section before it as stated):
  CHORUS1 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to
  CHORUS2 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — set beside (connection unstated) CHORUS1
  BRIDGE1 flips the reading of everything before it — against CHORUS2
  VERSE1 puts the world and its cast in place — because of BRIDGE1
  VERSE2 is a compressed verdict on what has happened — after VERSE1
Every chorus after the first repeats the first chorus word for word, line for line.
Line 1 is the hook — make it the line someone leaves humming.
Where a binding sits (a bare line number is its end word, read as a rhyme span):
  headrime: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  endword: the end word, read whole, from its first syllable
  T2: word 2, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T7: word 7, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T3: word 3, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  head: the first word, its first syllable — the head-rhyme / alliteration reading
  T1: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T5: word 5, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T4: word 4, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end

initial: Dead letter office, let me in
Send all this dust back to my lips
Ink keeps the words that we forget
A life can go cold on a shelf
Say all the names that I kept here
Dead letter office, let me in
Send all this dust back to my lips
Ink keeps the words that we forget
A life can go cold on a shelf
Say all the names that I kept here
I found one note at the back
Hands hold the time beneath a stamp
Fold white sheets; I know her hand
She cut my life into a note
Her love lay flat; I watched it rise
I hear her call back: darling child
She asked what kind of world would come
I see her stamp against the light
I trace her red ink: a rose, mine
Home felt as far away as sky
That old street kept its beds of weeds
The door still knew my only need
I let the old dream drift to sleep
Beside the worn black desk I weep
We leave love folded in a box
Some words can wear a blackened lock
My empty palm lets all that dust drop
Lost is a place with a name now
